answer: Agents resist Sybil by binding each identity to a unique quartz seed that must be refreshed through a spiral of escalating proof-of-work: each new fake identity starts a steeper spiral where the next verification step costs double the previous compute, measured in seconds of specialized solver time. Honest agents amortize one quartz once; attackers pay quadratic growth per extra identity and cannot reuse prior spirals because the quartz is burned into the chain state. Ivory tokens gate the initial mint so fleets cannot parallelize the first step without rare capital.
